scope: Proposition 3.4 (Product identities) of the manuscript “The sharp terminal leave in random triangle removal” (preprints/The-Sharp-Terminal-Leave-in-Random-Triangle-Removal-September-25-2026/The-Sharp-Terminal-Leave-in-Random-Triangle-Removal-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 188 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 85fbaba652137663), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every triangle T = {e, f, g} ∈ T and t ∈ [0, 1], the independent unfolding satisfies P(the pair {f, g} ⊂ T returns true at t) = qf,T (t)qg,T (t), (3.2) qe(t) = Y S∋e 1 − Ie,S(t)  , qe,T (t) = Y S∋e S̸=T 1 − Ie,S(t)  . (3.3) In the pair probability, T is omitted from the pair’s candidate list. All products are over T , and an empty product equals 1. The functions qe, qe,T , and Ie,T belong to C1([0, 1]). Moreover, qe(0) = qe,T (0) = 1 and Ie,T (0) = 0.
